messages:
sara.ng: Heads up — after yesterday's RBAC refactor I noticed a deploy CI token can call the node-proxy attach API and then get a KMS-encrypted key for GPU device mapping. This feels wrong. Can folks weigh in?

mike.k: ugh, that was part of my cleanup to reduce cluster-admin policies. I accidentally broadened the deploy-sa RoleBinding to include system:node-proxier group.

jordan.p: can you paste the binding?

mike.k: sure — here's the change in the diff:```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: deploy-runner-bind
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: deploy-runner
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: deploy-runner-sa
  namespace: ci
- kind: Group
  name: system:node-proxier  # ← accidentally added
```

olivia-r: that group gives permissions to call the attach/exec endpoints via the proxy layer, right?

mike.k: yes, which means deploy jobs could request attach sessions and then request the node to return the encrypted device token we use for GPU mapping.

sec-bot: [audit] 2026-03-09T15:12:02Z svc=deploy-runner-sa action=proxy.attach target=node-37 result=allowed token_subject=deploy-runner-sa

oncall-sre: we saw a spike in attach requests yesterday correlated with a CI job that iterated on many small GPU tests. Not catastrophic but noisy.

sara.ng: worst case is exfil of KMS-encrypted blobs tied to instance identity. We encrypt with customer KMS (just metadata), but the node policy decrypt path is sensitive. Need to confirm whether deploy-runner-sa can call KMS:Decrypt via IAM role on the node?

jordan.p: quick check of the node instance profile shows kms:Decrypt is allowed for project-node role, but only when assumed by instance identity. The risk is a pod using node-proxy to force the node to return the blob (already encrypted) and then some lateral step to decrypt if they can assume the node role.

mike.k: my immediate plan: revert the accidental group addition and push a patch to remove system:node-proxier from that binding. Also add an admission webhook test.

olivia-r: agree. Also we should add an audit alert rule: if a non-node SA performs proxy.attach to nodes, page sec oncall.

sec-bot: rule created: alert if subject not in system:nodes group calls proxy.attach (pending deploy).

oncall-sre: for mitigation, can we disable attach on CI namespace nodes temporarily? That will break some tests though.

sara.ng: avoid broad disable. Revert + patch + rotate deploy-runner-sa tokens. Also rotate KMS CMK grant to nodes to be safe (short window).

jordan.p: can we tighten the Role to only allow pod/exec to pods in the CI namespace rather than node-proxy? Example role rule:```yaml
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods/exec", "pods/portforward"]
  verbs: ["create"]
  resourceNames: null
```

mike.k: yep. I'll open a PR to: revert binding, scope Role to namespace-level pod exec, add unit test to the admission webhook forbidding system:node-proxier in deploy rolebindings, and trigger token rotation for deploy-runner-sa.

olivia-r: add a quick audit query to find any other RoleBindings that mention node-proxier — run `kubectl get rolebindings --all-namespaces -o yaml | grep -C3 node-proxier` and scan.

sara.ng: action items: 1) mike revert + scoped role PR (priority P0), 2) rotate deploy-runner-sa token and invalidate sessions (security), 3) add audit alert (olivia), 4) run grep scan for other bindings (jordan), 5) short CMK grant rotation window for nodes (infra ops).

mike.k: starting now. I'll post the PR link when ready.

sec-bot: note: this thread will be recorded in security incidents log (severity: low -> medium until resolved).

oncall-sre: if anything escalates ping me and I'll apply node taint to prevent new CI pods from scheduling on GPU nodes until fixed.

sara.ng: thanks team. Please keep replies short — want this deployed and tokens rotated within the hour. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
